content:
Alex: FYI - customer reported a sudden spike in 429s and an unexpected billing jump starting ~08:12 UTC. They say it started right after we pushed the limiter config change last night. attaching what they sent.
Maria: thanks for flagging. which customer / env?
Alex: acme-corp, dedicated region eu-west-1. their calls were normal until the deploy at 02:48 UTC.
Ian: this sounds like the quota domain mismatch we saw in staging last month where dedicated tenants inherited hosted burst rules. can you paste the limiter config they were given?
Alex: customer provided this snippet from their support token metadata (redacted keys):
```
X-Client-ID: acme-corp
X-API-Key: ****
RateLimit-Policy: tier_enterprise_v2
Burst-Capacity: 1000000
Refill-Rate: 5000/s
Quota-Window: 3600
Quota-Limit: 0  # ???
```
Alex: that Quota-Limit: 0 is suspicious — they claim they were previously on a committed reserved throughput plan with a per-hour quota.
Sam: 0 would effectively disable the quota enforcement in some of our code paths and let bursts exhaust downstream capacity. horrible edge-case.
Maria: can you share sample 429 stack traces or gateway logs?
Alex: pasted from our gateway logs (sanitized):
```
[08:14:06] upstream_write_timeout - token_bucket overflow - key=acme-corp:global - tokens_deducted=54000 - remaining=-52000
[08:14:07] rate_limiter.apply error: quota window exceeded but bucket still had positive burst
[08:14:08] response 429 -> client=acme-corp - route=/v1/generate - latency=720ms
```
Ian: looks like two issues: (1) quota-limit 0 caused our quota-check short-circuit to return "not-enforced" in the hosted path, then (2) burst capacity allowed huge instantaneous drains that hit downstream GPU pools and triggered fallback -> more 429s. we need to confirm the code path that uses Quota-Limit.
Sam: I'll grep the runtime repo for quota-limit==0 handling.
OpsBot: @oncall SRE assigned: @Ian (escalation).
Ian: oncall here. immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the limiter config change globally, 2) push a per-tenant override to set quota to their committed value, 3) throttle at edge (nginx) to smooth bursts.
Maria: rollback seems fastest. do we know which deployment included the bad defaults?
Alex: rollout label: limiter-config-2026-03-14-v3. it was a templating change to the policy generator.
Sam: found code: templates/limits.tmpl had an inadvertent default_quota = 0 fallback when tenant_metadata is empty. reproducer found.
Ian: ok rollback plan: revert limiter-config to v2, redeploy config generator, and trigger config refresh on all dedicated clusters. Also add a temporary ip-based rate-limit for acme-corp to stop immediate pressure.
Alex: acme-corp says they can tolerate a short rollback + throttle if done within 30 minutes. they are grateful.
Maria: who will perform the rollback and the per-tenant override?
Sam: I can push the rollback PR and coordinate deploy. planning 08:40 UTC.
Ian: I'll prepare a per-tenant override: set Quota-Limit=360000 (100 req/s * 3600s) and Burst-Capacity=10000. also enable additional alerting for rate-limit delta > 10x.
OpsBot: deploy queued: limiter-config revert -> 08:42 UTC by Sam. CI checks green.
Sam: rollback completed at 08:45 UTC. config refresh triggered.
Alex: confirms 429 rate downtrend in our metrics: 08:46 -> 08:55 drop from 18% to 0.8% of requests. billing spike paused.
Maria: nice work. next steps for post-incident: - write a short incident note - add unit test for default_quota fallback - add e2e test that simulates burst against dedicated tenant - update policy templating docs - run a customer-facing RCA draft with Acme
Ian: I'll own the postmortem and the tests. will include a timeline and the specific code link to templates/limits.tmpl PR#5487.
Sam: I'll open the rollback PR and the per-tenant override cleanup ticket (support-1227).
Alex: customer requested a small change: make a visible flag in console showing "active quota overrides" for dedicated tenants. filing feature request.
Maria: good. also add an alert for quota-limit==0 in the config generator pipeline so a pre-deploy check fails.
Ian: logging decision: emit telemetry metric limiter.quota_default_zero{tenant} when default_quota==0 so it surfaces in dashboards.
OpsBot: Incident resolution logged -> severity: high; key action items assigned.
Alex: leaving final note for handoff: please ensure billing team inspects the spike for any one-off invoices; mark this customer as "compensate" candidate until we confirm amounts.
Maria: acknowledged. I'll loop in billing and CS.
Ian: postmortem ETA: end of day EOD today.
Sam: closing thread once postmortem link is up. :thumbsup:
